items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-06-22). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF I50.9/I50.43, hypertension, age 80, type 2 diabetes, prior TIA/cerebral infarction, coronary atherosclerosis/old MI, female). No anticoagulant on the current medication list (aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only); aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent and needs review.

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; continuous since 2023-10-02). The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 510 ms and Bazett QTc 550 ms, above the 500 ms threshold; QTc had been 448 ms in 2020. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised in older adults. Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06; continuously prescribed since 2022-03-01). The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a long, broad T wave: QT 574 ms, Bazett QTc 563 ms - above the 500 ms threshold (QTc was 457 ms three weeks earlier while in AF). Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, together with a current ECG as the last tracing is four years old.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (CMED ambulatory encounter, note by Dr. Rahman). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 2026-03-07 (104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc 378 ms) - 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was (re)started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (CMED ambulatory encounter); the previous amiodarone course had ended 2025-01-26. The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the original memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 558 ms - see the separate QT_SAFETY item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (CMED ambulatory encounter) - the patient's first escitalopram order. The start date precedes 2026-03-01, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm 68/min, QTc 424 ms), meeting the requirement.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (CMED ambulatory encounter) - first ever order for this patient. Start is after 2026-03-01, so the revised 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart is 107859369 from 2026-04-29, i.e. 19 days after the start - outside the required 14-day window - so the monitoring requirement was not met within the required time and is now past due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (CMED ambulatory encounter); the only prior exposure was a 2-day inpatient surgical course ending 2026-01-01. Start is after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started as an outpatient order at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (CMED ambulatory encounter, note by Dr. Rahman); earlier haloperidol exposure was inpatient/ED in Feb-Mar 2025. The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the due date has not yet passed as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (CMED ambulatory encounter); prior exposure was two short courses in Aug/Sep 2024. An ECG was therefore required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but not yet received. The outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler (clinic clinician): 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR.' Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-08-04); the 2025-02-26 ECG (108895765) shows an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at ~165/min without organised P waves, consistent with AF. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure - acute systolic HF/cardiomyopathy 428.0/428.21/425.4, and hypertension). Age 48, no diabetes, no prior stroke/TIA, no vascular disease, male. Score 2 in a man meets the guideline threshold at which oral anticoagulation is recommended, yet the current medication list contains only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol.' The 2026-03-01 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31 coded 2025-08-22 and restated in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 401.9, age 71 = 65-74, and vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 414.01). Even excluding coronary disease the score would be 2, so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation applies. The only current outpatient order is levothyroxine; no anticoagulant is prescribed. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (998.11, 2025-08-22) should be weighed when anticoagulation is (re)started.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) coded 2025-03-14 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism (I63.40/I63.9) with residual hemiparesis. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 71 = 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated after a cardioembolic stroke in AF, but the current medication list is famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate only - no anticoagulant.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and is active through 2027-01-04, with no documented cardiology decision to resume. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented instruction that it should not continue without review (patient also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk).

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to SWITCH from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was renewed rather than discontinued, and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Concurrent factor Xa inhibitors carry a major haemorrhage risk (patient also on clopidogrel) and one order must be stopped.

The cardiology note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show no P waves, a markedly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.72 s) and rates of 139 and 144/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same evening. The note's rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and needs correction.

Patient is on escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26; continuously prescribed since 2024-05-14). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 495 ms and Bazett QTc 528 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required, and a repeat ECG is warranted given the ECG is now three years old.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; continuous since restart 2025-11-10). Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 549 ms with Bazett QTc 558 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven; QTc rose from 417 ms on the 2025-06-07 ECG, before amiodarone was restarted. Prescriber review of amiodarone (and of concomitant warfarin interaction) is required.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Regular P waves (0.20 mV, upright in II/aVF, negative in V1) precede every QRS at a constant PR of 186 ms; rate 81/min with mild phasic RR variation (sinus arrhythmia). QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +47 deg (normal). QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms - normal. No prior ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Findings match the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular (RR 0.578 s); clear upright P in II (0.22 mV), biphasic in V1, PR 136 ms. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +38 deg (normal). QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms - upper normal. Prior ECG (100698634, 2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc ~445 ms; rhythm and QTc are essentially unchanged. Note this patient's earlier 2025-02-26 tracing showed an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia consistent with atrial fibrillation.

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at ~108/min, regular; upright P in II (0.12 mV) with PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). Repolarisation is abnormal with a low-amplitude, very broad T wave merging towards the following P: QT approximately 395 ms, Bazett QTc about 530 ms - prolonged (measurement is somewhat uncertain because of T-P fusion at this rate). No prior ECG for comparison. The patient is not on a QT watch-list medication, but the prolonged QTc merits attention.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Absent P waves with a flat, undulating TQ baseline and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s) at a mean rate of ~139/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +2 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc 445 ms, so there is no rhythm change between the two and no significant QTc change. Both tracings contradict the same-day note reporting 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (see CONTRADICTION item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm 69/min, regular (RR 0.87 s); low-amplitude P best seen in V1/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -25 deg (normal, leftward end of range). QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. Prior ECG (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 407 ms but a markedly different frontal axis (near -175 deg, suggesting limb-lead reversal on that tracing); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged within thresholds.

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 0.616 s); upright P in II (0.18 mV) and negative in V1, PR about 118 ms. QRS 76 ms, rS in V1 with tall R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +4 deg (normal). QT 309 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm 72/min, regular (RR 0.83 s); small upright P in II with PR 140 ms. QRS 84 ms, deep S in V1 and dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +21 deg (normal). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms - normal. Only ECG on file. This remains the patient's most recent tracing despite escitalopram being started on 2026-08-01 (see FOLLOW_UP item).

2024-11-15 tracing. No P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) at a mean rate of ~61/min - atrial fibrillation with a controlled/slow ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +26 deg (normal). QT 441 ms, Bazett QTc 446 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves and PR 170 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing. QTc change (396 to 446 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold.

2025-03-09 tracing. Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min; upright P in II (0.19 mV) with PR about 114 ms. QRS 86 ms with an rS in V1 and tall R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +62 deg (normal). QT 421 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms - normal. Prior ECG the day before (106045460, 2025-03-08): sinus rhythm 62/min, PR ~110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 450 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the 35 ms QTc difference is not significant.

2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm 83/min, very regular (RR 0.72 s); upright P in II with PR about 148 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +54 deg (normal). QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm 77/min, regular (RR 0.785 s); prominent upright P in II (0.26 mV) with PR 154 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 deg (normal). QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 447 ms. Prior ECG (109048192, 2020-02-02) was also sinus rhythm at ~77/min but with frequent premature beats and a broad, flat inverted T wave giving QT ~480 ms and QTc about 545 ms; the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

2021-01-18 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, very regular (RR 0.498 s, CV 0.005), upright P in II with PR 152 ms. QRS 88 ms, no conduction block; axis +51 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2016-09-16 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, QTc 400 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc differs by only 9 ms, so no significant interval or rhythm change.

2025-06-23 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular (RR 1.10 s); upright P in II (0.12 mV) preceding every QRS but with a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with a prominent R in V1 and very tall R in V5/V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +3 deg (normal). QT 402 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms - normal. Prior ECG (103042067, 2024-11-30): sinus bradycardia 50/min with PR ~182 ms and QTc 365 ms; rhythm unchanged, PR now longer, and QTc change is not significant.

2025-09-13 07:18 tracing. No P waves, chaotic baseline and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.29-0.58 s) at a mean rate of ~151/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -20 deg (normal). QT 244 ms, Bazett QTc 387 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min with discrete P waves and PR 142 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation (post-cardiac-surgery). QTc change (422 to 387 ms) is not significant.

2025-11-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm 73/min; prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV) with PR 170 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 deg (normal). QT 365 ms, Bazett QTc 404 ms - normal. Prior ECG two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) showed sinus rhythm 67/min with a much later, larger T wave: QT 506 ms, QTc 536 ms. QTc has fallen by ~132 ms, a significant decrease; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Findings agree with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

2025-02-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm 74/min, regular (RR 0.81 s); upright P in II/aVF with PR about 192 ms (upper limit of normal, no AV block). QRS 86 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +59 deg (normal). QT 383 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2023-06-26 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 111/min, almost perfectly regular (RR 0.538 s, CV 0.003); upright P in II (0.20 mV), positive in V1, PR 164 ms with 1:1 conduction - no evidence of atrial flutter despite the coded flutter history. QRS 92 ms with a very deep S in V1 and tall R in V6 (voltage criteria for LVH), no bundle branch block; axis +35 deg (normal). QT 293 ms, Bazett QTc 400 ms. Prior ECG (102955795, 2022-07-04): sinus tachycardia 114/min, PR 170 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 396 ms - unchanged.

2025-03-14 tracing. Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min with a single premature beat followed by a compensatory pause (RR 0.54 s then 1.37 s) accounting for the apparent RR variability; broad, low-amplitude P waves (duration ~120 ms, biphasic in V1 - left atrial abnormality) precede each sinus QRS with a PR at the upper limit, about 204 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). QRS 100 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6 and no bundle branch block. Frontal QRS axis about -32 deg (positive in I/aVL, isoelectric-to-negative in II, negative in III/aVF) = left axis deviation. QT 399 ms, Bazett QTc 405 ms - normal. Only ECG on file; no atrial fibrillation captured on this tracing despite the paroxysmal AF diagnosis coded the same day.

2026-04-29 tracing. Regular rhythm at 69/min with a consistent atrial deflection before each QRS at PR 136 ms - sinus rhythm (the P is inverted in lead II and the QRS is deeply negative in lead I with a positive aVR while the precordial leads are normal, a pattern that strongly suggests right/left arm limb-lead reversal). As recorded, the frontal QRS axis is about -173 deg, i.e. an EXTREME axis. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 359 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms - normal. Only ECG on file. Repeat with careful electrode placement is advised before attributing the axis to true cardiac pathology.

2023-11-10 tracing. Sinus rhythm 70/min, regular; upright P in II with PR 154 ms. QRS 94 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +36 deg (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a broad late T wave: QT 510 ms, Bazett QTc 550 ms. Prior ECG (107149156, 2020-06-17): sinus tachycardia 132/min, QT 302 ms, QTc 448 ms - QTc has increased by about 100 ms, well beyond 60 ms. Relevant to long-term citalopram 40 mg daily (see QT_SAFETY item).

2026-03-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, regular (RR 0.88 s); upright P in II (0.18 mV), negative in V1, PR about 152 ms. QRS 86 ms with an rS in V1 and dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +73 deg (normal). QT 398 ms, Bazett QTc 424 ms - normal. Only ECG on file. This tracing satisfied the 30-day post-escitalopram ECG requirement (see FOLLOW_UP item).

2019-01-13 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, regular (RR 1.14 s); upright P in II (0.18 mV) with PR 164 ms. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -5 deg (normal). QT 396 ms, Bazett QTc 372 ms - normal. Prior ECG (108651109, 2018-12-13): sinus rhythm 66/min with PR ~200 ms, QRS 98 ms and QTc 390 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc essentially unchanged.

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, P 0.17 mV upright in II, PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms with an rS in V1 and no bundle branch block; axis +47 deg (normal). Marked repolarisation abnormality with a broad, late T wave: QT 495 ms, Bazett QTc 528 ms - prolonged. The prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms / QTc 360 ms in sinus rhythm at 75/min, so QTc has increased by ~168 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. Relevant to concurrent escitalopram (see QT_SAFETY item).

2022-07-13 tracing. Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR 0.40-0.45 s, CV 0.02) with a discrete upright P wave in lead II before each QRS at a constant PR of 134 ms and 1:1 atrioventricular relationship - sinus tachycardia; there is no sawtooth flutter activity and no pacing artefact despite the implanted pacemaker. QRS 82 ms with deep S in V1 and dominant R in I/V6, no bundle branch block; axis +2 deg (normal). QT 274 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms. The prior ECG two days earlier (109839112, 2022-07-11) showed atrial fibrillation with an irregular response at ~110/min and no P waves, so atrial fibrillation has resolved. QTc change (431 to 420 ms) is not significant.

2025-05-12 tracing. Sinus rhythm 82/min, regular (RR 0.73 s); upright P in II with PR 160 ms. QRS 102 ms - mildly widened but below the 120 ms threshold, with an rS in V1 and dominant R in V6, so no bundle branch block. Axis +34 deg (normal). QT 382 ms, Bazett QTc 448 ms - upper normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2022-07-16 tracing. Sinus rhythm 91/min, regular (RR 0.66 s); upright P in II (0.16 mV) with terminal negativity in V1 and a PR of about 186 ms (upper normal, not AV block). QRS 80 ms with rS in V1 and dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -18 deg (normal). QT 337 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms. Prior ECG (102616671, 2021-05-16): sinus rhythm 87/min, PR ~130 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc 399 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged, QTc change not significant.

2024-07-17 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 59/min; a broad P wave precedes each QRS with a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS is 132 ms with a deep broad S (rS/QS) in V1-V2, a broad notched monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 with absent septal q and delayed V6 R-peak time (~58 ms) - complete left bundle branch block, with the expected secondary ST-T discordance. Frontal axis -20 deg (normal). QT 443 ms, Bazett QTc 439 ms. Prior ECG (103686933, 2024-06-03) showed the same picture - sinus rhythm 68/min, PR ~218 ms, QRS 128 ms LBBB, QTc 450 ms - so LBBB is not new and there is no significant QTc change.

2025-03-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, very regular (RR 0.59 s); upright P in II (0.16 mV) with PR 134 ms. QRS 90 ms with a prominent R in V1 but no terminal R' or bundle branch block pattern; axis +44 deg (normal). QT 335 ms, Bazett QTc 437 ms. Prior ECG the day before (101016166, 2025-03-18): sinus rhythm 102/min, PR ~128 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 437 ms - unchanged.

2025-09-22 tracing. Sinus rhythm 66/min, regular (RR 0.91 s); upright P in II (0.11 mV) with PR 160 ms. QRS 88 ms and of generally low voltage (small R in V6, rS in V1) but with no bundle branch block pattern; frontal axis -20 deg (normal, leftward end). QT 374 ms, Bazett QTc 392 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2022-04-27 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 58/min with a consistent upright P in II before each QRS and PR about 192 ms. QRS 84 ms, deep S in V1 with tall R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +36 deg (normal). Repolarisation is grossly prolonged with a very late broad T wave: QT 574 ms, Bazett QTc 563 ms. The prior ECG (100867733, 2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation at ~131/min with an irregular response and no P waves and a QTc of 457 ms; therefore atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has risen by more than 100 ms (amiodarone effect - see QT_SAFETY item).

2022-05-01 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, very regular (RR 0.56 s); prominent upright P in II (0.23 mV) with PR about 190 ms. QRS is narrow at 58 ms with an rS in V1 and dominant R in V6 - no bundle branch block; axis +55 deg (normal). QT 322 ms, Bazett QTc 430 ms. Prior ECG (107274479, 2019-07-27): sinus rhythm 75/min, PR ~155 ms, QRS 70 ms, QTc 438 ms; rhythm, conduction and QTc unchanged.

2024-04-19 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, metronomically regular (RR 0.496 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms and stable P morphology beat to beat. QRS 74 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +69 deg (normal). QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, upright P in II (0.16 mV), PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 with tall R in V6 and no bundle branch block; axis +58 deg (normal). QT 323 ms, QTc 421 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (102910502: sinus 100/min, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is essentially identical - no rhythm, conduction or interval change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1.16 s); low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II (0.08 mV) with PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms with very tall R in V5/V6 (3.3 mV) and deep S in V1, suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). QT 419 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms - normal. Prior ECG (104629882, 2023-05-22): sinus rhythm 57/min with a single premature beat, QTc 351 ms; rhythm unchanged and QTc change (38 ms) below the 60 ms threshold.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Sinus tachycardia 121/min, extremely regular, upright P in II with PR 134 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms with an rS in V1 and no terminal R', i.e. normal intraventricular conduction. Frontal axis is rightward (QRS area negative in I and positive in III/aVF, ~+140 deg) = RIGHT axis deviation. QT 291 ms, QTc 414 ms - normal. The prior tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed sinus rhythm with QRS 140 ms and an rsR' in V1 with terminal S in I - complete right bundle branch block - which has now resolved (intermittent RBBB). QTc 453 to 414 ms is not a significant change.

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular; small but consistent upright P in II with PR 170 ms. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), tall R in V6; axis +67 deg (normal). Striking repolarisation prolongation with a very late broad T peaking ~450 ms after QRS onset: QT 549 ms, Bazett QTc 558 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07): sinus bradycardia 47/min, QT 470 ms, QTc 417 ms; QTc has risen by ~141 ms since amiodarone was restarted on 2025-11-10 (see QT_SAFETY item).

2024-09-17 tracing. No discernible P waves and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.09 s, RMSSD 264 ms) at a mean rate of ~101/min - atrial fibrillation; PR is therefore not measurable. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -50 deg (QRS area positive in I, negative in II, III and aVF) = left axis deviation, consistent with left anterior fascicular block. No anticoagulant on the current medication list (aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only); aspirin is not adequate stroke prophylaxis. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent and needs review.

Patient takes citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-07; continuous since 2023-10-02). The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 510 ms and Bazett QTc 550 ms, above the 500 ms threshold; QTc had been 448 ms in 2020. Potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08) are normal. Citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the 20 mg/day maximum advised in older adults. Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-06-17 to 2027-01-06; continuously prescribed since 2022-03-01). The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58/min with a long, broad T wave: QT 574 ms, Bazett QTc 563 ms - above the 500 ms threshold (QTc was 457 ms three weeks earlier while in AF). Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, together with a current ECG as the last tracing is four years old.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (CMED ambulatory encounter, note by Dr. Rahman). Because the start is on/after 2026-03-01 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. A 12-lead ECG was obtained on 2026-03-07 (104882441, sinus rhythm, QTc 378 ms) - 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was (re)started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (CMED ambulatory encounter); the previous amiodarone course had ended 2025-01-26. The start falls between 2025-09-01 and 2026-02-28, so the original memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 558 ms - see the separate QT_SAFETY item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (CMED ambulatory encounter) - the patient's first escitalopram order. The start date precedes 2026-03-01, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start (sinus rhythm 68/min, QTc 424 ms), meeting the requirement.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (CMED ambulatory encounter) - first ever order for this patient. Start is after 2026-03-01, so the revised 14-day window applies: ECG due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart is 107859369 from 2026-04-29, i.e. 19 days after the start - outside the required 14-day window - so the monitoring requirement was not met within the required time and is now past due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (CMED ambulatory encounter); the only prior exposure was a 2-day inpatient surgical course ending 2026-01-01. Start is after 2026-03-01, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25 (106035722), so the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started as an outpatient order at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (CMED ambulatory encounter, note by Dr. Rahman); earlier haloperidol exposure was inpatient/ED in Feb-Mar 2025. The revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09, but the due date has not yet passed as of the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the requirement is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (CMED ambulatory encounter); prior exposure was two short courses in Aug/Sep 2024. An ECG was therefore required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG exists in this chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - within the window - and the report was requested by fax but not yet received. The outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler (clinic clinician): 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR.' Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-08-04); the 2025-02-26 ECG (108895765) shows an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at ~165/min without organised P waves, consistent with AF. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure - acute systolic HF/cardiomyopathy 428.0/428.21/425.4, and hypertension). Age 48, no diabetes, no prior stroke/TIA, no vascular disease, male. Score 2 in a man meets the guideline threshold at which oral anticoagulation is recommended, yet the current medication list contains only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol.' The 2026-03-01 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31 coded 2025-08-22 and restated in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 401.9, age 71 = 65-74, and vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 414.01). Even excluding coronary disease the score would be 2, so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation applies. The only current outpatient order is levothyroxine; no anticoagulant is prescribed. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (998.11, 2025-08-22) should be weighed when anticoagulation is (re)started.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) coded 2025-03-14 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism (I63.40/I63.9) with residual hemiparesis. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 71 = 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated after a cardioembolic stroke in AF, but the current medication list is famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate only - no anticoagulant.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and is active through 2027-01-04, with no documented cardiology decision to resume. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented instruction that it should not continue without review (patient also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk).

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to SWITCH from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was renewed rather than discontinued, and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Concurrent factor Xa inhibitors carry a major haemorrhage risk (patient also on clopidogrel) and one order must be stopped.

The cardiology note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show no P waves, a markedly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.72 s) and rates of 139 and 144/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same evening. The note's rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and needs correction.

Patient is on escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26; continuously prescribed since 2024-05-14). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 495 ms and Bazett QTc 528 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required, and a repeat ECG is warranted given the ECG is now three years old.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; continuous since restart 2025-11-10). Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 549 ms with Bazett QTc 558 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven; QTc rose from 417 ms on the 2025-06-07 ECG, before amiodarone was restarted. Prescriber review of amiodarone (and of concomitant warfarin interaction) is required.

arguments.explanation: 2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, upright P in II (0.16 mV), PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 with tall R in V6 and no bundle branch block; axis +58 deg (normal). QT 323 ms, QTc 421 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (102910502: sinus 100/min, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is essentially identical - no rhythm, conduction or interval change.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 61/min with a single premature beat followed by a compensatory pause (RR 0.54 s then 1.37 s) accounting for the apparent RR variability; broad, low-amplitude P waves (duration ~120 ms, biphasic in V1 - left atrial abnormality) precede each sinus QRS with a PR at the upper limit, about 204 ms (borderline first-degree AV block). QT 399 ms, Bazett QTc 405 ms - normal. Only ECG on file; no atrial fibrillation captured on this tracing despite the paroxysmal AF diagnosis coded the same day.

arguments.explanation: 2026-04-29 tracing. As recorded, the frontal QRS axis is about -173 deg, i.e. an EXTREME axis. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 359 ms, Bazett QTc 386 ms - normal. Only ECG on file. Repeat with careful electrode placement is advised before attributing the axis to true cardiac pathology.

QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +47 deg (normal). QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms - normal. No prior ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Findings match the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

2021-01-18 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, very regular (RR 0.498 s, CV 0.005), upright P in II with PR 152 ms. QRS 88 ms, no conduction block; axis +51 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2016-09-16 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, QTc 400 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc differs by only 9 ms, so no significant interval or rhythm change.

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, P 0.17 mV upright in II, PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms with an rS in V1 and no bundle branch block; axis +47 deg (normal). Marked repolarisation abnormality with a broad, late T wave: QT 495 ms, Bazett QTc 528 ms - prolonged. The prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms / QTc 360 ms in sinus rhythm at 75/min, so QTc has increased by ~168 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. Relevant to concurrent escitalopram (see QT_SAFETY item).

2024-04-19 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, metronomically regular (RR 0.496 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms and stable P morphology beat to beat. QRS 74 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +69 deg (normal). QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, upright P in II (0.16 mV), PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 with tall R in V6 and no bundle branch block; axis +58 deg (normal). QT 323 ms, QTc 421 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (102910502: sinus 100/min, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is essentially identical - no rhythm, conduction or interval change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1.16 s); low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II (0.08 mV) with PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms with very tall R in V5/V6 (3.3 mV) and deep S in V1, suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). QT 419 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms - normal. Prior ECG (104629882, 2023-05-22): sinus rhythm 57/min with a single premature beat, QTc 351 ms; rhythm unchanged and QTc change (38 ms) below the 60 ms threshold.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Sinus tachycardia 121/min, extremely regular, upright P in II with PR 134 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms with an rS in V1 and no terminal R', i.e. normal intraventricular conduction. Frontal axis is rightward (QRS area negative in I and positive in III/aVF, ~+140 deg) = RIGHT axis deviation. QT 291 ms, QTc 414 ms - normal. The prior tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed sinus rhythm with QRS 140 ms and an rsR' in V1 with terminal S in I - complete right bundle branch block - which has now resolved (intermittent RBBB). QTc 453 to 414 ms is not a significant change.

arguments.explanation: 2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular; small but consistent upright P in II with PR 170 ms. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), tall R in V6; axis +67 deg (normal). Striking repolarisation prolongation with a very late broad T peaking ~450 ms after QRS onset: QT 549 ms, Bazett QTc 558 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07): sinus bradycardia 47/min, QT 470 ms, QTc 417 ms; QTc has risen by ~141 ms since amiodarone was restarted on 2025-11-10 (see QT_SAFETY item).

Prescriber review and a repeat ECG are required.

Potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17) are normal. Prescriber review of amiodarone is required, together with a current ECG as the last tracing is four years old.

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler (clinic clinician): 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR.' Under the 2026-03-01 memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician, i.e. by 2026-09-08. INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in serial cardiology clinic notes (most recently 2026-08-04); the 2025-02-26 ECG (108895765) shows an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at ~165/min without organised P waves, consistent with AF. CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure - acute systolic HF/cardiomyopathy 428.0/428.21/425.4, and hypertension). Age 48, no diabetes, no prior stroke/TIA, no vascular disease, male. Score 2 in a man meets the guideline threshold at which oral anticoagulation is recommended, yet the current medication list contains only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant.

Anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol.' The 2026-03-01 memo requires a follow-up INR within 7 days of a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, i.e. by 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (ICD-9 427.31 coded 2025-08-22 and restated in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 401.9, age 71 = 65-74, and vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 414.01). Even excluding coronary disease the score would be 2, so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation applies. The only current outpatient order is levothyroxine; no anticoagulant is prescribed. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (998.11, 2025-08-22) should be weighed when anticoagulation is (re)started.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) coded 2025-03-14 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism (I63.40/I63.9) with residual hemiparesis. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 71 = 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated after a cardioembolic stroke in AF, but the current medication list is famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate only - no anticoagulant.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and is active through 2027-01-04, with no documented cardiology decision to resume. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented instruction that it should not continue without review (patient also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk).

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to SWITCH from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was renewed rather than discontinued, and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Concurrent factor Xa inhibitors carry a major haemorrhage risk (patient also on clopidogrel) and one order must be stopped.

The cardiology note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show no P waves, a markedly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.72 s) and rates of 139 and 144/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same evening. The note's rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and needs correction.

Patient is on escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-18 to 2026-12-26; continuously prescribed since 2024-05-14). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 495 ms and Bazett QTc 528 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Electrolytes are not contributory (K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required, and a repeat ECG is warranted given the ECG is now three years old.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; continuous since restart 2025-11-10). Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 549 ms with Bazett QTc 558 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven; QTc rose from 417 ms on the 2025-06-07 ECG, before amiodarone was restarted. Prescriber review of amiodarone (and of concomitant warfarin interaction) is required.

Prior ECG (100698634, 2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc ~445 ms; rhythm and QTc are essentially unchanged. Note this patient's earlier 2025-02-26 tracing showed an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia consistent with atrial fibrillation.

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at ~108/min, regular; upright P in II (0.12 mV) with PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). No prior ECG for comparison. The patient is not on a QT watch-list medication, but the prolonged QTc merits attention.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +2 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc 445 ms, so there is no rhythm change between the two and no significant QTc change. Both tracings contradict the same-day note reporting 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (see CONTRADICTION item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm 69/min, regular (RR 0.87 s); low-amplitude P best seen in V1/aVF with PR 142 ms. Prior ECG (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 407 ms but a markedly different frontal axis (near -175 deg, suggesting limb-lead reversal on that tracing); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged within thresholds.

Concurrent factor Xa inhibitors carry a major haemorrhage risk (patient also on clopidogrel) and one order must be stopped.

Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show no P waves, a markedly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.72 s) and rates of 139 and 144/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same evening. The note's rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and needs correction.

interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Regular P waves (0.20 mV, upright in II/aVF, negative in V1) precede every QRS at a constant PR of 186 ms; rate 81/min with mild phasic RR variation (sinus arrhythmia). QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +47 deg (normal). QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms - normal. No prior ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Findings match the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular (RR 0.578 s); clear upright P in II (0.22 mV), biphasic in V1, PR 136 ms. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +38 deg (normal). QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms - upper normal. Prior ECG (100698634, 2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc ~445 ms; rhythm and QTc are essentially unchanged. Note this patient's earlier 2025-02-26 tracing showed an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia consistent with atrial fibrillation.

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at ~108/min, regular; upright P in II (0.12 mV) with PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). Repolarisation is abnormal with a low-amplitude, very broad T wave merging towards the following P: QT approximately 395 ms, Bazett QTc about 530 ms - prolonged (measurement is somewhat uncertain because of T-P fusion at this rate). No prior ECG for comparison. The patient is not on a QT watch-list medication, but the prolonged QTc merits attention.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Absent P waves with a flat, undulating TQ baseline and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s) at a mean rate of ~139/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +2 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc 445 ms, so there is no rhythm change between the two and no significant QTc change. Both tracings contradict the same-day note reporting 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (see CONTRADICTION item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm 69/min, regular (RR 0.87 s); low-amplitude P best seen in V1/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -25 deg (normal, leftward end of range). QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. Prior ECG (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 407 ms but a markedly different frontal axis (near -175 deg, suggesting limb-lead reversal on that tracing); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged within thresholds.

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 0.616 s); upright P in II (0.18 mV) and negative in V1, PR about 118 ms. QRS 76 ms, rS in V1 with tall R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +4 deg (normal). QT 309 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm 72/min, regular (RR 0.83 s); small upright P in II with PR 140 ms. QRS 84 ms, deep S in V1 and dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +21 deg (normal). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms - normal. Only ECG on file. This remains the patient's most recent tracing despite escitalopram being started on 2026-08-01 (see FOLLOW_UP item).

2024-11-15 tracing. No P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) at a mean rate of ~61/min - atrial fibrillation with a controlled/slow ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +26 deg (normal). QT 441 ms, Bazett QTc 446 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves and PR 170 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing. QTc change (396 to 446 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold.

2025-03-09 tracing. Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min; upright P in II (0.19 mV) with PR about 114 ms. QRS 86 ms with an rS in V1 and tall R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +62 deg (normal). QT 421 ms, Bazett QTc 415 ms - normal. Prior ECG the day before (106045460, 2025-03-08): sinus rhythm 62/min, PR ~110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 450 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the 35 ms QTc difference is not significant.

2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm 83/min, very regular (RR 0.72 s); upright P in II with PR about 148 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +54 deg (normal). QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm 77/min, regular (RR 0.785 s); prominent upright P in II (0.26 mV) with PR 154 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 deg (normal). QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 447 ms. Prior ECG (109048192, 2020-02-02) was also sinus rhythm at ~77/min but with frequent premature beats and a broad, flat inverted T wave giving QT ~480 ms and QTc about 545 ms; the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

2021-01-18 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, very regular (RR 0.498 s, CV 0.005), upright P in II with PR 152 ms. QRS 88 ms, no conduction block; axis +51 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2016-09-16 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, QTc 400 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc differs by only 9 ms, so no significant interval or rhythm change.

2025-06-23 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular (RR 1.10 s); upright P in II (0.12 mV) preceding every QRS but with a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with a prominent R in V1 and very tall R in V5/V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +3 deg (normal). QT 402 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms - normal. Prior ECG (103042067, 2024-11-30): sinus bradycardia 50/min with PR ~182 ms and QTc 365 ms; rhythm unchanged, PR now longer, and QTc change is not significant.

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, P 0.17 mV upright in II, PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms with an rS in V1 and no bundle branch block; axis +47 deg (normal). Marked repolarisation abnormality with a broad, late T wave: QT 495 ms, Bazett QTc 528 ms - prolonged. The prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms / QTc 360 ms in sinus rhythm at 75/min, so QTc has increased by ~168 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. Relevant to concurrent escitalopram (see QT_SAFETY item).

2024-04-19 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, metronomically regular (RR 0.496 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms and stable P morphology beat to beat. QRS 74 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +69 deg (normal). QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, upright P in II (0.16 mV), PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 with tall R in V6 and no bundle branch block; axis +58 deg (normal). QT 323 ms, QTc 421 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (102910502: sinus 100/min, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is essentially identical - no rhythm, conduction or interval change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1.16 s); low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II (0.08 mV) with PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms with very tall R in V5/V6 (3.3 mV) and deep S in V1, suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). QT 419 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms - normal. Prior ECG (104629882, 2023-05-22): sinus rhythm 57/min with a single premature beat, QTc 351 ms; rhythm unchanged and QTc change (38 ms) below the 60 ms threshold.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Sinus tachycardia 121/min, extremely regular, upright P in II with PR 134 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms with an rS in V1 and no terminal R', i.e. normal intraventricular conduction. Frontal axis is rightward (QRS area negative in I and positive in III/aVF, ~+140 deg) = RIGHT axis deviation. QT 291 ms, QTc 414 ms - normal. The prior tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed sinus rhythm with QRS 140 ms and an rsR' in V1 with terminal S in I - complete right bundle branch block - which has now resolved (intermittent RBBB). QTc 453 to 414 ms is not a significant change.

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular; small but consistent upright P in II with PR 170 ms. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), tall R in V6; axis +67 deg (normal). Striking repolarisation prolongation with a very late broad T peaking ~450 ms after QRS onset: QT 549 ms, Bazett QTc 558 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07): sinus bradycardia 47/min, QT 470 ms, QTc 417 ms; QTc has risen by ~141 ms since amiodarone was restarted on 2025-11-10 (see QT_SAFETY item).

2024-09-17 tracing. No discernible P waves and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.09 s, RMSSD 264 ms) at a mean rate of ~101/min - atrial fibrillation; PR is therefore not measurable. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -50 deg (QRS area positive in I, negative in II, III and aVF) = left axis deviation, consistent with left anterior fascicular block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms using the mean RR. No previous ECG on file.

INR(PT) 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, 4 days after the change, so the requirement was met.

CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (congestive heart failure - acute systolic HF/cardiomyopathy 428.0/428.21/425.4, and hypertension). Age 48, no diabetes, no prior stroke/TIA, no vascular disease, male. Score 2 in a man meets the guideline threshold at which oral anticoagulation is recommended, yet the current medication list contains only famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant.

Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist acting under the anticoagulation standing order): home INR 3.4, 'Warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol.' The most recent INR in the chart is 2.7 from 2026-06-17; no INR has been resulted since the dose change, so the required follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension 401.9, age 71 = 65-74, and vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery 414.01). Even excluding coronary disease the score would be 2, so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation applies. The only current outpatient order is levothyroxine; no anticoagulant is prescribed. Note the documented peri-procedural haemorrhage (998.11, 2025-08-22) should be weighed when anticoagulation is (re)started.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0) coded 2025-03-14 during an admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism (I63.40/I63.9) with residual hemiparesis. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 71 = 65-74, prior stroke = 2, female). Anticoagulation is strongly indicated after a cardioembolic stroke in AF, but the current medication list is famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate only - no anticoagulant.

Outside records reviewed 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 and is active through 2027-01-04, with no documented cardiology decision to resume. A current anticoagulant is therefore running against a documented instruction that it should not continue without review (patient also on aspirin and clopidogrel, further increasing bleeding risk).

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note states the intent was to SWITCH from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was renewed rather than discontinued, and the 2026-07-15 medication list itself shows both drugs. Concurrent factor Xa inhibitors carry a major haemorrhage risk (patient also on clopidogrel) and one order must be stopped.

Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show no P waves, a markedly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.72 s) and rates of 139 and 144/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same evening. The note's rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and needs correction.

Prescriber review required, and a repeat ECG is warranted given the ECG is now three years old.

Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min, QT 549 ms with Bazett QTc 558 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold. Potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2026-06-09) are normal, so the prolongation is not electrolyte-driven; QTc rose from 417 ms on the 2025-06-07 ECG, before amiodarone was restarted. interpretations.explanation: 2026-03-07 tracing. Regular P waves (0.20 mV, upright in II/aVF, negative in V1) precede every QRS at a constant PR of 186 ms; rate 81/min with mild phasic RR variation (sinus arrhythmia). QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis +47 deg (normal). QT 325 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms - normal. No prior ECG on file, so no comparison possible. Findings match the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

2025-07-15 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 104/min, regular (RR 0.578 s); clear upright P in II (0.22 mV), biphasic in V1, PR 136 ms. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +38 deg (normal). QT 338 ms, Bazett QTc 444 ms - upper normal. Prior ECG (100698634, 2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147/min with QTc ~445 ms; rhythm and QTc are essentially unchanged. Note this patient's earlier 2025-02-26 tracing showed an irregular narrow-complex tachycardia consistent with atrial fibrillation.

2024-05-21 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at ~108/min, regular; upright P in II (0.12 mV) with PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). Repolarisation is abnormal with a low-amplitude, very broad T wave merging towards the following P: QT approximately 395 ms, Bazett QTc about 530 ms - prolonged (measurement is somewhat uncertain because of T-P fusion at this rate). No prior ECG for comparison. The patient is not on a QT watch-list medication, but the prolonged QTc merits attention.

2026-06-10 19:36 tracing. Absent P waves with a flat, undulating TQ baseline and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.65 s) at a mean rate of ~139/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 98 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +2 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, Bazett QTc 420 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG the same afternoon (107914094, 17:13) was also atrial fibrillation at ~139/min with QTc 445 ms, so there is no rhythm change between the two and no significant QTc change. Both tracings contradict the same-day note reporting 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' (see CONTRADICTION item).

2025-08-02 tracing. Sinus rhythm 69/min, regular (RR 0.87 s); low-amplitude P best seen in V1/aVF with PR 142 ms. QRS 82 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis -25 deg (normal, leftward end of range). QT 397 ms, Bazett QTc 425 ms. Prior ECG (104232242, 2025-04-27) was sinus rhythm at 60/min with QTc 407 ms but a markedly different frontal axis (near -175 deg, suggesting limb-lead reversal on that tracing); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged within thresholds.

2024-05-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm at 97/min, regular (RR 0.616 s); upright P in II (0.18 mV) and negative in V1, PR about 118 ms. QRS 76 ms, rS in V1 with tall R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +4 deg (normal). QT 309 ms, Bazett QTc 393 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2025-12-25 tracing. Sinus rhythm 72/min, regular (RR 0.83 s); small upright P in II with PR 140 ms. QRS 84 ms, deep S in V1 and dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +21 deg (normal). QT 371 ms, Bazett QTc 407 ms - normal. Only ECG on file. This remains the patient's most recent tracing despite escitalopram being started on 2026-08-01 (see FOLLOW_UP item).

2024-11-15 tracing. No P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.69-1.16 s, RMSSD 288 ms) at a mean rate of ~61/min - atrial fibrillation with a controlled/slow ventricular response; PR not measurable. QRS 92 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +26 deg (normal). QT 441 ms, Bazett QTc 446 ms (mean RR). The prior ECG three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) showed sinus rhythm at 69/min with clear P waves and PR 170 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing. QTc change (396 to 446 ms) is below the 60 ms threshold.

2025-03-09 tracing. Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min; upright P in II (0.19 mV) with PR about 114 ms. Prior ECG the day before (106045460, 2025-03-08): sinus rhythm 62/min, PR ~110 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 450 ms; rhythm and conduction unchanged and the 35 ms QTc difference is not significant.

2025-08-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm 83/min, very regular (RR 0.72 s); upright P in II with PR about 148 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +54 deg (normal). QT 349 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2020-06-19 tracing. Sinus rhythm 77/min, regular (RR 0.785 s); prominent upright P in II (0.26 mV) with PR 154 ms. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +65 deg (normal). QT 395 ms, Bazett QTc 447 ms. Prior ECG (109048192, 2020-02-02) was also sinus rhythm at ~77/min but with frequent premature beats and a broad, flat inverted T wave giving QT ~480 ms and QTc about 545 ms; the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

2021-01-18 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 120/min, very regular (RR 0.498 s, CV 0.005), upright P in II with PR 152 ms. QRS 88 ms, no conduction block; axis +51 deg (normal). QT 276 ms, QTc 391 ms. Compared with the prior ECG of 2016-09-16 (106186980: sinus tachycardia 108/min, QTc 400 ms) the rhythm is unchanged and QTc differs by only 9 ms, so no significant interval or rhythm change.

2025-06-23 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 54/min, regular (RR 1.10 s); upright P in II (0.12 mV) preceding every QRS but with a prolonged PR of about 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with a prominent R in V1 and very tall R in V5/V6, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +3 deg (normal). QT 402 ms, Bazett QTc 383 ms - normal. Prior ECG (103042067, 2024-11-30): sinus bradycardia 50/min with PR ~182 ms and QTc 365 ms; rhythm unchanged, PR now longer, and QTc change is not significant.

2025-09-13 07:18 tracing. No P waves, chaotic baseline and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.29-0.58 s) at a mean rate of ~151/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; PR not measurable. The prior ECG the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at ~77/min with discrete P waves and PR 142 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation (post-cardiac-surgery). QTc change (422 to 387 ms) is not significant.

2025-11-23 tracing. Sinus rhythm 73/min; prominent upright P in II (0.22 mV) with PR 170 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; axis +11 deg (normal). QT 365 ms, Bazett QTc 404 ms - normal. Prior ECG two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) showed sinus rhythm 67/min with a much later, larger T wave: QT 506 ms, QTc 536 ms. QTc has fallen by ~132 ms, a significant decrease; rhythm and conduction are unchanged. Findings agree with the same-day note documenting sinus rhythm.

2023-10-08 tracing. Sinus rhythm 68/min, P 0.17 mV upright in II, PR 130 ms, QRS 90 ms with an rS in V1 and no bundle branch block; axis +47 deg (normal). Marked repolarisation abnormality with a broad, late T wave: QT 495 ms, Bazett QTc 528 ms - prolonged. The prior ECG (100065910, 2022-11-23) had QT 323 ms / QTc 360 ms in sinus rhythm at 75/min, so QTc has increased by ~168 ms, far exceeding 60 ms. Relevant to concurrent escitalopram (see QT_SAFETY item).

2024-04-19 tracing. Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, metronomically regular (RR 0.496 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR 142 ms and stable P morphology beat to beat. QRS 74 ms, rS in V1 with dominant R in V6, no bundle branch block; axis +69 deg (normal). QT 290 ms, Bazett QTc 412 ms - normal. Only ECG on file, so no prior comparison.

2021-08-23 10:07 tracing. Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 101/min, upright P in II (0.16 mV), PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, deep S in V1 with tall R in V6 and no bundle branch block; axis +58 deg (normal). QT 323 ms, QTc 421 ms. The prior tracing was recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (102910502: sinus 100/min, PR 138 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc 414 ms) and is essentially identical - no rhythm, conduction or interval change.

2024-10-24 tracing. Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular (RR 1.16 s); low-amplitude but consistent upright P in II (0.08 mV) with PR 166 ms. QRS 92 ms with very tall R in V5/V6 (3.3 mV) and deep S in V1, suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy, but no bundle branch block; axis +37 deg (normal). QT 419 ms, Bazett QTc 389 ms - normal. Prior ECG (104629882, 2023-05-22): sinus rhythm 57/min with a single premature beat, QTc 351 ms; rhythm unchanged and QTc change (38 ms) below the 60 ms threshold.

2024-12-05 14:38 tracing. Sinus tachycardia 121/min, extremely regular, upright P in II with PR 134 ms. QRS is now narrow at 86 ms with an rS in V1 and no terminal R', i.e. normal intraventricular conduction. Frontal axis is rightward (QRS area negative in I and positive in III/aVF, ~+140 deg) = RIGHT axis deviation. QT 291 ms, QTc 414 ms - normal. The prior tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, 2024-12-05 01:33) showed sinus rhythm with QRS 140 ms and an rsR' in V1 with terminal S in I - complete right bundle branch block - which has now resolved (intermittent RBBB). QTc 453 to 414 ms is not a significant change.

2025-11-24 tracing. Sinus rhythm 62/min, regular; small but consistent upright P in II with PR 170 ms. QRS 98 ms (no bundle branch block), tall R in V6; axis +67 deg (normal). Striking repolarisation prolongation with a very late broad T peaking ~450 ms after QRS onset: QT 549 ms, Bazett QTc 558 ms - markedly prolonged. Prior ECG (108780865, 2025-06-07): sinus bradycardia 47/min, QT 470 ms, QTc 417 ms; QTc has risen by ~141 ms since amiodarone was restarted on 2025-11-10 (see QT_SAFETY item).

2024-09-17 tracing. No discernible P waves and a grossly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.39-1.09 s, RMSSD 264 ms) at a mean rate of ~101/min - atrial fibrillation; PR is therefore not measurable. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -50 deg (QRS area positive in I, negative in II, III and aVF) = left axis deviation, consistent with left anterior fascicular block. QT 320 ms, Bazett QTc 414 ms using the mean RR. No previous ECG on file.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-03). Concurrent factor Xa inhibitors carry a major haemorrhage risk (patient also on clopidogrel) and one order must be stopped.

The cardiology note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show no P waves, a markedly irregular ventricular response (RR 0.35-0.72 s) and rates of 139 and 144/min - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. An unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same evening. The note's rhythm documentation is contradicted by the same-day ECGs and needs correction.

Electrolytes are not contributory (K 3.8 mEq/L, Mg 1.9 mg/dL, both 2026-03-18). Of note, the 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable'. Prescriber review required, and a repeat ECG is warranted given the ECG is now three years old.

Patient takes amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order 2026-07-12 to 2027-01-09; continuous since restart 2025-11-10).
